dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:2901.text: 籧篨, a coarse bamboo mat. Formed from 竹, with 遽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2902.text: The coarse bamboo mat 籧篨. Formed from 竹, with 除 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2903.text: A bamboo implement that retains coarse material and removes fine material. Formed from 竹, with 麗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2904.text: A large winnowing basket. Formed from 竹, with 潘 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a screen.

shuowen:2905.text: A sieve for draining rice. Formed from 竹, with 奥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2906.text: A cooking sieve, 䉛. Formed from 竹, with 數 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2907.text: A covering used to cover the bottom of a steamer. Formed from 竹, with 𢌿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2908.text: A rice basket holding five sheng. Formed from 竹, with 稍 indicating the sound. Qin calls the 筥 𥳓.

shuowen:2909.text: In Chenliu, a rice brush is called 䈰. Formed from 竹, with 捎 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a rice vessel holding five sheng; another: Song and Wei call a chopstick tube 䈰.

shuowen:2910.text: The vessel 䈰. Formed from 竹, with 呂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2911.text: A container for rice and clothing. Formed from 竹, with 司 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2912.text: A container, 笥. Formed from 竹, with 單 indicating the sound. Han ford ordinances: 簞 is a small basket. The Commentary says: “A basket of food and a jug of drink.”

shuowen:2913.text: 簁箄, a bamboo implement. Formed from 竹, with 徙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2914.text: The bamboo implement 簁箄. Formed from 竹, with 卑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2915.text: A round bamboo implement. Formed from 竹, with 專 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2916.text: An implement for lifting rice. Formed from 竹, with 者 indicating the sound. [The gloss 飯攲 is uncertain.]

shuowen:2917.text: A bamboo basket. Formed from 竹, with 婁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2918.text: A basket, 籃. Formed from 竹, with 良 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2919.text: A large basket frame, 篝. Formed from 竹, with 監 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2920.text: A basket frame, 笿, usable for perfuming clothes. Formed from 竹, with 冓 indicating the sound. In Song and Chu, a bamboo frame used as an enclosure for dwelling is called 篝.

shuowen:2921.text: A basket for cups. Formed from 竹, with 各 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2922.text: A basket for cups. Formed from 竹, with 夅 indicating the sound. Some say a basket holding chopsticks.

shuowen:2923.text: A mirror case. Formed from 竹, with 斂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2924.text: A bamboo implement. Formed from 竹, with 贊 indicating the sound. Read like 纂. Another explanation: a cluster.

shuowen:2925.text: A basket or case, 笭. Formed from 竹, with 贏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2926.text: A bamboo implement. Formed from 竹, with 𠛹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2927.text: A square vessel for millet. From 竹, 皿 and 皀.

shuowen:2928.text: A round vessel for millet. Formed from 竹 and 皿, with 甫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2929.text: A bamboo pedestal dish. Formed from 竹, with 邊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2930.text: The grain container 篅. Formed from 竹, with 屯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2931.text: A round container made of split bamboo for holding grain. Formed from 竹, with 耑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2932.text: A tall bamboo chest. Formed from 竹, with 鹿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2933.text: A large bamboo tube. Formed from 竹, with 昜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2934.text: A cut section of bamboo. Formed from 竹, with 甬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2935.text: A bamboo carriage or litter. Formed from 竹, with 便 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2936.text: A bird cage. Formed from 竹, with 奴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2937.text: A bamboo pole. Formed from 竹, with 干 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2938.text: An implement for trapping fish beneath a cover. Formed from 竹, with 靃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2939.text: One piece of bamboo. Formed from 竹, with 固 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2940.text: A bamboo rope. Formed from 竹, with 交 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2941.text: A bamboo rope, 筊. Formed from 竹, with 作 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2942.text: A mat covering padding. Formed from 竹, with 沾 indicating the sound. Read like 錢.

shuowen:2943.text: A fan. Formed from 竹, with 疌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2944.text: A vessel for carrying earth. Another explanation: a basket, 笭. Formed from 竹, with 龍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2945.text: A carrying basket or wrapping container, 袌. Formed from 竹, with 襄 indicating the sound. [The exact object is uncertain.]

shuowen:2946.text: That which can wind up rope. From 竹, pictographic; the middle depicts what a hand pushes and grasps.

shuowen:2947.text: A bamboo vessel holding meat in ancestral temples. Formed from 竹, with 尞 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “Provide basins and 簝 to await service.”

shuowen:2948.text: A basket for watering cattle. Formed from 竹, with 豦 indicating the sound. Square ones are 筐; round ones are 𥴧.

shuowen:2949.text: A vessel for watering horses. Formed from 竹, with 兜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2950.text: Layered bamboo shafts for spears and halberds. Formed from 竹, with 盧 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Discourses of the States says: “A dwarf supports the 籚.”

shuowen:2951.text: Pincers, 籋. Formed from 竹, with 拑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2952.text: Pincers, 箝. Formed from 竹, with 爾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2953.text: A canopy like a broad hat. Formed from 竹, with 登 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2954.text: A 簦 without a handle, a hat. Formed from 竹, with 立 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2955.text: The receiving compartment of a large cart. Formed from 竹, with 相 indicating the sound. [The vehicle term 牝服 is uncertain.]

shuowen:2956.text: A carriage basket or rail. Formed from 竹, with 匪 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2957.text: A carriage basket or rail. Formed from 竹, with 令 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a case, 籯.

shuowen:2958.text: To curry a horse. Formed from 竹, with 剡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2959.text: A horsewhip. Formed from 竹, with 朿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2960.text: To strike a horse. Formed from 竹, with 𡍮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2961.text: A whip. Formed from 竹, with 朵 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2962.text: The driver's whip for a sheep-drawn carriage, with a needle half a fen long fixed at its tip. Formed from 竹, with 内 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2963.text: A container for crossbow bolts, carried on a person's back. Formed from 竹, with 闌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2964.text: A crossbow-bolt case. Formed from 竹, with 服 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “In mid-autumn present arrows and cases.”

shuowen:2965.text: The object 栙雙, apparently a bamboo sail or frame. Formed from 竹, with 朱 indicating the sound. [The rare gloss is uncertain.]

shuowen:2966.text: A rod of split bamboo. Formed from 竹, with 占 indicating the sound. Yingchuan people call the tablets children write on 笘.

shuowen:2967.text: To beat with a bamboo rod. Formed from 竹, with 旦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2968.text: To strike. Formed from 竹, with 台 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2969.text: To verify. Another explanation: sharp; to pierce through. Formed from 竹, with 韱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2970.text: A board or placard. Formed from 竹, with 殿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2971.text: A needle for stitching clothing. Formed from 竹, with 咸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2972.text: To strike a person with a pole. Formed from 竹, with 削 indicating the sound. The music of Shun of Yu was called 箾韶.

shuowen:2973.text: A pipe instrument with thirty-six reeds. Formed from 竹, with 亏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2974.text: Thirteen reeds, resembling a phoenix's body. 笙 is the sound of the first month; things are born then, hence its name. The large is called 巢, the small 和. Formed from 竹, with 生 indicating the sound. Anciently Sui made the 笙.

shuowen:2975.text: The reed inside a 笙. Formed from 竹, with 黃 indicating the sound. Anciently Nüwa made the 簧.

shuowen:2976.text: A kind of reed instrument. Formed from 竹, with 是 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2977.text: A musical instrument of pipes of unequal lengths, resembling a phoenix's wings. Formed from 竹, with 肅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2978.text: A through-pipe flute. Formed from 竹, with 同 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2979.text: A three-holed pipe: the large is called 笙, the middle 籟, the small 箹. Formed from 竹, with 賴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2980.text: A small 籟 pipe. Formed from 竹, with 約 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2981.text: Like a 篪, with six holes. The sound of the twelfth month, when things open the earth and sprout, hence called 管. Formed from 竹, with 官 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2982.text: A small pipe is called 篎. Formed from 竹, with 眇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2983.text: A seven-holed tube. Formed from 竹, with 由 indicating the sound. The Qiang flute has three holes.

shuowen:2984.text: A five-stringed musical instrument with bent bamboo. From 竹 and 𢀜; 𢀜 means to hold it. 竹 also supplies the sound.

shuowen:2985.text: A musical instrument with plucked strings and a bamboo body. Formed from 竹, with 爭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2986.text: A blowing tube called 吹鞭. Formed from 竹, with 孤 indicating the sound. [The exact instrument is uncertain.]

shuowen:2987.text: A tube to blow into. Formed from 竹, with 秋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2988.text: Arrows used in pitch-pot. Formed from 竹, with 壽 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2989.text: Moving game pieces so as to block one another is called 簺. Formed from 竹 and 塞, with 塞 also indicating the sound.

shuowen:2990.text: A board game with six throwing rods and twelve pieces. Formed from 竹, with 博 indicating the sound. Anciently Wuzhou invented it.

shuowen:2991.text: A fence. Formed from 竹, with 畢 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “A wicker gate and a narrow opening.”

shuowen:2992.text: To cover so something cannot be seen. Formed from 竹, with 愛 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2993.text: A screen used when shooting with corded arrows. Formed from 竹, with 嚴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2994.text: A restricted park. Formed from 竹, with 御 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “The marsh's 目篽.” [The quoted expression is uncertain.]

shuowen:2995.text: Six inches long, used for calendrical calculations. From 竹 and 弄: only through constant handling does one avoid errors.

shuowen:2996.text: To calculate. From 竹 and 具. Read like 筭.

shuowen:2998.text: A small room beside an upper gallery. Formed from 竹, with 移 indicating the sound. The Shuowen also uses 誃.

shuowen:2999.text: The skin of bamboo. Formed from 竹, with 均 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3000.text: What dukes and scholars tuck into their belts. Formed from 竹, with 勿 indicating the sound. Note: the large-seal form is 𡇉, pictographic. Its meaning is “worn at the belt”; anciently the 笏 was worn there. This character was added by later people.
